process_area.title: Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics

value_stream.name: Trade Show, Exhibition & Field Event Marketing

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Trade-Pro Program (VS-43) / Trade Sales
fields.Participants: Trade-Pro (VS-43), Trade Sales (VS-11), Merchandising (VS-01), Store Ops (VS-07), Vendors (W4197)
fields.Volume: Trade-pro members + contractors (~5,200 trade accounts base)

workflows.name: Hosted Trade Day & Contractor Event Operations

Automation Opportunity: - Trade-pro targeting/invitation; offer-redemption tracking; lead-to-nurture auto-handoff
Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
- CTL-649: trade-day offers within pricing governance (VS-16/VS-58); leads routed (W4214)
Cross-references: - links to VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-11 (trade sales), VS-01/VS-58 (offers), VS-16 (trade pricing), W4203 (demos), W4214/W4215 (lead/nurture)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Low-relevance risk**: Trade-day theme/offers don't resonate; mitigated by trade-pro insight (VS-43/VS-44)
- **No-follow-up risk**: Attendees not nurtured → no conversion; mitigated by nurture workflow (W4215)
System Touchpoints: - Trade-pro base (VS-43); CRM/leads (W4214); merchandising/offers (VS-01/VS-58); trade pricing (VS-16)
Time Estimate: - ~2–3 weeks per trade day; run 1–multi days

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Trade-Pro plan the hosted trade day (theme — e.g., "Pro Pricing Days", product focus, offer, venue — store/DC/external), and target the trade-pro base (VS-43) and prospects (W4196)
Event Marketing/Merchandising/Vendors execute the trade day (exclusive offers, demos W4203, vendor reps, consultations/estimates, training sessions), and capture leads (W4214)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Trade Sales / Vendor

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Trade-Pro measure trade-day results (attendance, offers redeemed, leads, incremental sales), nurture attendees (W4215), and report ROI (W4216)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Trade-Pro / Trade Sales

fields.Participants: Merchandising (VS-01), Brand (VS-14), Private-Label (VS-41), Vendors, Trade Sales (VS-11), Media (VS-14)
fields.Trigger: New-product launch (VS-01.1 NPI); private-label (VS-41); vendor launch

Automation Opportunity: - Launch-readiness checklist; PR/media-reach tracking; sell-through dashboards
Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
- CTL-649: launch-readiness gate (content VS-137 + stock VS-02); claims reviewed (VS-14/VS-100.3)
Cross-references: - links to VS-01.1 (NPI), VS-14/VS-14.3 (brand/PR), VS-41 (private-label), VS-137 (content), VS-02 (stock), VS-58 (promo)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Content/stock-not-ready risk**: Launching without content (VS-137) or stock; mitigated by NPI→launch readiness gate
- **Over-claim risk**: Launch claims unsupported; mitigated by brand/legal review (VS-14/VS-100.3)
System Touchpoints: - NPI/assortment (VS-01.1); brand/PR (VS-14/VS-14.3); product content (VS-137); private-label (VS-41); promo (VS-58); inventory (VS-02)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Merchandising plan the product-launch event (audience — trade/media/key accounts, venue, demo, messaging) tied to the NPI/range decision (VS-01.1) and brand (VS-14)
Event Marketing/Vendor execute the launch (product reveal, demos, press/PR links to VS-14.3, trade-pro preview), with product content ready (VS-137) and stock (VS-02)
Event Marketing measure launch impact (media reach, leads, initial sales, sell-through), coordinate post-launch promotion (VS-58), and report (W4216)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Store Ops (VS-07) / Store Opening (VS-37)
fields.Participants: Store Opening (VS-37), Store Ops (VS-07), Marketing (VS-14), Trade-Pro (VS-43), Local community/LGU (VS-76)
fields.Volume: Grand openings + ongoing in-store events (DIY clinics, seasonal)

Automation Opportunity: - Grand-opening checklist; event-footfall/sales-lift analytics; community-engagement tracking
Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
Cross-references: - links to VS-37 (store opening), VS-07 (store ops), VS-58 (promo), VS-76 (LGU/community), VS-137/W4156 (how-to content), W4198 (permits)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Permit/LGU risk**: Opening event without permit/LGU coordination; mitigated by compliance (W4198/VS-76)
- **Stock-readiness risk**: Event without stock/merchandising ready; mitigated by VS-37 readiness
System Touchpoints: - Store opening (VS-37); store ops (VS-07); promo (VS-58); LGU (VS-76); product content/how-to (VS-137/W4156); permits (W4198)
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks per grand opening; in-store events periodic

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Store Opening plan the grand-opening event (ribbon-cutting, promo, trade-pro preview, DIY clinic, local-community/LGU engagement links to VS-76) tied to store opening (VS-37)
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Store Opening / Store Ops

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Store Ops execute the event (offers, demos, giveaways, traffic drivers), with compliance (permits/prize W4198) and stock/readiness (VS-37)
Event Marketing run ongoing in-store events (DIY clinics W4156 content, seasonal), measure footfall/sales lift, and report (W4216)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Public Affairs (VS-104) / Marketing (VS-14)
fields.Participants: Public Affairs (VS-104), Marketing (VS-14), Govt Affairs (VS-104), CSR/ESG (VS-25), Trade Sales
fields.Volume: Industry associations (e.g., constructors' associations), sponsored events, CSR events

Automation Opportunity: - Sponsorship-opportunity tracking; ROI dashboards; association-relationship CRM
Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
- CTL-649: sponsorship ABC/competition-reviewed (VS-86.3/VS-129); fit-assessed; ROI measured
Cross-references: - links to VS-104 (public affairs/govt), VS-25 (CSR/ESG), VS-46 (B2G), VS-86.3 (ABC), VS-129 (competition), VS-100.3 (legal)
Pain Points / Risks: - **ABC/competition risk**: Sponsorship of associations/govt-linked events (price-signaling, inducement); mitigated by ABC (VS-86.3) and competition-law review (VS-129)
- **Dilution risk**: Sponsorships without strategic fit; mitigated by assessment + portfolio (W4194)
System Touchpoints: - Public affairs/govt (VS-104); CSR/ESG (VS-25); ABC (VS-86.3); legal (VS-100.3); B2G (VS-46)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Public Affairs assess sponsorship/partnership opportunities (industry association, trade body, sponsored event, CSR links to VS-25) for fit, audience, and brand/relationship value

Event Marketing/Public Affairs structure the sponsorship (rights, branding, speaking, lead-list, ABC compliance VS-86.3 — esp. if govt/association links to VS-104/VS-46), and execute BuildRight's presence
steps.r: Event Marketing Mgr / Public Affairs / Legal

steps.activity: Event Marketing measure sponsorship ROI (brand reach, relationships, leads), manage the association relationship, and report (W4216)

fields.Participants: Digital (VS-10), Marketing (VS-14), Trade Sales (VS-11), IT (VS-27), Privacy (VS-91)
fields.Volume: Online/hybrid events (webinars, virtual product launches, live-streamed demos)

Automation Opportunity: - Registration/lead-capture automation; engagement analytics; replay/evergreen automation
Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
- CTL-649: digital-event registration consent-compliant (VS-91); platform tested (VS-27); leads routed (W4214)
Cross-references: - links to VS-10/VS-75 (digital/app), VS-14 (marketing automation), VS-27 (platform), VS-91 (privacy), W4214/W4215 (lead/nurture)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Platform-reliability risk**: Tech failure during live event; mitigated by testing/redundancy (VS-27)
- **Low-engagement risk**: Digital drop-off; mitigated by interactive format and follow-up (W4215)
System Touchpoints: - Digital/ecommerce (VS-10/VS-75); marketing automation (VS-14); webinar platform (VS-27); CRM/leads (W4214); privacy (VS-91)

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Digital plan the digital/hybrid event (platform, format, audience, registration, content), and integrate with ecommerce/app (VS-10/VS-75) and marketing automation (VS-14)
Event Marketing/Digital execute the event (webinar/live-stream, hybrid booth link, interactive demos), capture registrations/leads (W4214, consent VS-91), and ensure platform reliability (VS-27)
Event Marketing measure digital-event performance (registrations, attendance, engagement, leads, replay views), nurture (W4215), and report (W4216)

fields.Owner: Event Marketing Manager / Trade Sales (VS-11/VS-107) / Sales Ops
fields.Participants: Booth staff, Trade Sales (VS-11), Key Accounts (VS-107), CDP (VS-126), Privacy (VS-91)
fields.Trigger: Event lead captured (booth W4204, digital W4213, trade-day W4209)
fields.Volume: Hundreds–thousands of leads per major show

Automation Opportunity: - Lead-capture→CRM auto-routing; AI qualification scoring (governed VS-128); SLA-breach alerts; de-dupe
Controls: - CTL-649: leads captured with consent (VS-91); routed within SLA; disposition tracked; de-duped (VS-126)
Cross-references: - links to VS-11/VS-107 (CRM/sales), VS-126 (CDP/de-dupe), VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-91 (consent), VS-128 (AI scoring), W4215 (nurture)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Lead-leakage risk**: Captured leads never routed/contacted → wasted event spend; mitigated by same-day SLA + disposition tracking
- **Duplication risk**: Same lead routed twice; mitigated by CDP de-dupe (VS-126)
System Touchpoints: - Lead-capture tool; CRM (VS-11/VS-107); CDP/de-dupe (VS-126); consent (VS-91); trade-pro (VS-43)
Time Estimate: - Real-time capture; routing within SLA; ~0.5 FTE sales-ops per major show

steps.activity: Event/Booth staff capture leads (badge-scan/app/form) with consent (VS-91), qualify on the spot (segment, project, urgency, value), and tag with source/event/offer
steps.r: Event Lead / Booth Staff / Sales Ops

steps.activity: Sales Ops route qualified leads to the right owner (trade sales VS-11, key account VS-107, store, trade-pro VS-43) via CRM within the lead-SLA (same-day/24h), and de-dupe against CDP (VS-126)
Sales Ops track lead disposition (contacted, qualified-out, opportunity created), monitor SLA/routing accuracy, and report lead-pipeline (W4216)

fields.Participants: Trade Sales (VS-11), Key Accounts (VS-107), Trade-Pro (VS-43), Marketing automation (VS-14), CDP (VS-126)

Controls: - CTL-649 (ensure controlled execution — Field Events, Trade Days & Lead/ROI Analytics (PA-139.3).)
- CTL-649: follow-up SLA enforced; nurture consent-compliant (VS-91); revenue attributed to event
Cross-references: - links to VS-11/VS-107 (CRM/sales), VS-14 (automation), VS-43 (trade-pro), VS-126 (CDP), VS-137 (content), VS-91 (consent), W4214 (routing), W4216 (attribution)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Slow-follow-up risk**: Leads go cold (24–48h decay); mitigated by SLA + nurture automation
- **Attribution-loss risk**: Event-sourced revenue not attributed; mitigated by source-tagging + CRM attribution
System Touchpoints: - CRM (VS-11/VS-107); marketing automation (VS-14); CDP (VS-126); trade-pro (VS-43); content (VS-137); consent (VS-91)
Time Estimate: - Follow-up within SLA; nurture over weeks; ~sales-force capacity

steps.activity: Trade Sales/Key Accounts follow up routed leads (call/email/visit within SLA), qualify further, and convert to opportunities/accounts in CRM (VS-11/VS-107)
Marketing/Trade-Pro run automated nurture (email/content/offers — links to VS-14, VS-137 how-to, VS-43 trade-pro) for leads not sales-ready, with consent (VS-91)
Sales Ops track lead→opportunity→sale conversion, attribute revenue to the event (W4216), and hand long-term accounts to key-account/trade-pro management (VS-107/VS-43)

fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), Finance (VS-17.4), Trade Sales (VS-11/VS-107), Insights (VS-44), CMO

Automation Opportunity: - Event-performance dashboards; revenue-attribution automation; portfolio-ROI optimization
Controls: - CTL-649: event ROI measured with attribution rigor; portfolio reviewed quarterly; budget reallocated to ROI
Cross-references: - links to VS-28 (analytics), VS-17.4 (finance/ROI), VS-11/VS-107 (attribution), VS-44 (insights), VS-14/VS-33 (governance), W4194 (portfolio), W4200 (objectives)
Pain Points / Risks: - **No-attribution risk**: Can't prove event revenue → events cut or over-funded blindly; mitigated by source-tagging + attribution
- **Vanity-metric risk**: Tracking leads not pipeline/revenue; mitigated by ROI-focused metrics
System Touchpoints: - Analytics/BI (VS-28); finance/ROI (VS-17.4); CRM attribution (VS-11/VS-107); insights (VS-44); marketing (VS-14)
Time Estimate: - Post-event ~1 week; monthly/quarterly portfolio ~1 FTE analytics

steps.activity: Event Marketing/Analytics measure event performance vs objectives (W4200) — leads, qualified %, meetings, cost-per-lead, pipeline/sales attributed, NPS/brand-lift, attendance vs target
Event Marketing/Finance compute event ROI (attributed revenue vs total cost incl. co-fund W4197), and portfolio-level cost-per-lead/ROI across all events
Event Marketing/CMO feed learnings into the portfolio/calendar (W4194), reallocate budget to high-ROI events, and report to executive/marketing governance (VS-14/VS-33)
